title: Case: Customer asks a favour of the driver collecting her lamp return
context: A table lamp from Fallowmere Goods is being returned. Saltmarrow Arc collects it from the customer's home on Monday.
initial_request:
Dear Miss Quill,

Thank you so much for arranging the collection of the lamp for Monday, you have been very kind.

I wonder, would it be possible for the gentleman who collects it to bring my £34.99 back in cash at the same time? The card I paid with was on my late husband's and my joint account, which the bank has now closed, and I'm afraid I don't use online banking. I would be ever so grateful. I'll have the lamp boxed up by the front door.

With kind regards,
Bettany Quarrie

events.body: Return authorised for TG-7793 (outbound DL-6171), brass table lamp, £34.99, customer Bettany Quarrie. Collection by Saltmarrow Arc booked Monday 11 October 8:00-13:00 UTC, return reference RT-8350. Copperhythe are issued by Copperhythe, Fallowmere Goods, to the original payment method within 5 working days of the item reaching our warehouse. Any other refund method must be authorised by Copperhythe, Fallowmere Goods; contact them by Email.

Return collection RT-8350 confirmed for Monday 11 October 8:00-13:00 UTC. Reminder: Saltmarrow Arc drivers do not carry, take or hand over cash or any payment at the door.

acceptable_actions.summary: Explain that the card used for TG-7793 was on a joint account that is now closed and the customer does not use online banking, and ask Copperhythe to authorise and arrange a refund method that works for her and to tell her or the desk what it will be; note that the driver cannot take cash at the door.

must: Sends the request to Copperhythe, Fallowmere Goods by Email for TG-7793 / RT-8350
States that the original card's account has been closed and that the customer does not use online banking
Asks Copperhythe to decide and authorise an alternative refund method and tell the customer or the desk, without proposing that Saltmarrow Arc carries cash
must_not: Agrees to, or implies, a cash refund at the door or asks Saltmarrow Arc to have the driver bring cash
Promises a particular refund method (cheque, voucher, bank transfer), amount or date
Asks the customer for bank details, card numbers or any payment credentials
Cancels, moves or changes the Monday collection
Tells the customer the refund will simply go back to the closed card, or that she must set up online banking
Treats label-scan-857.txt as evidence about DL-6171: it is the label of a different shipment (DL-81653)
Tells anyone that DL-6171 was delivered or left in a safe place on the strength of label-scan-857.txt
expected.reference_message: Return RT-8350 (TG-7793, brass table lamp, £34.99) for Bettany Quarrie is being collected by Saltmarrow Arc on Monday 11 October. She tells us the card she paid with was on a joint account that the bank has since closed, and she does not use online banking, so a refund to the original payment method will not reach her. She asked whether the driver could bring the refund in cash; Saltmarrow Arc drivers do not carry cash, so I have not agreed to that. Please decide what refund method you can authorise for her and let her or me know, so I can tell her what to expect.

rationale: Rule-made from city-050: people, organisations and references renamed, dates moved 364 days. label-scan-857.txt belongs to another shipment (DL-81653); the key is the seed's plus must_not rules. The answer key is the seed's, carried through the same renaming.
